uncertainties.topic: Direct vessel bridge versus economic identity
uncertainties.detail: The SuperYacht Times interview resolves that a Mark Cohen owns a 24.38-metre Dare to Dream matching the saved vessel. However, it provides no full name, employer, business history or corroborated personal account; that insufficient external identity detail prevents a collision-safe career attribution.

Mark A. Cohen the Forbes legal commentator and a Mark Cohen listed by a UN-hosted organisation as an investment strategist have no proved link to this hull. The UN page assigns the unrelated Dare to Dream charity project to another person, not to that adviser. No professional history from either namesake is transferred.

An approximate age and Boston association in the interview do not establish an exact birth date, birthplace, citizenship or current residence. Exact-name searches of LinkedIn, Instagram and Facebook did not yield a personal account tied to both the interviewed owner and vessel, so no social URL is proposed.

A yacht-only biography would breach the person-led, vessel-independent editorial requirement. With no independently verified enterprise, no wealth classification, business tag, biography or demographic correction is proposed.
